title: Patch: pin the perf corpus so card additions stop re-dealing it

**Issue #4924 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #4924: Patch: pin the perf corpus so card additions stop re-dealing it
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The engine-speed budgets the pull-request gate holds would stop wobbling every time cards ship. Today adding one card re-deals every game the perf corpus times, so medians jump for reasons that have nothing to do with the change under test, and someone has to re-measure the budgets by hand. After this change the corpus is a checked-in set of pinned games, so the same build always times the same games and a budget crossing means the code got slower.

## Why

`crates/tools/src/perf.rs` builds its corpus live on every run: plain golden seeds `PERF_SEED_FIRST..=PERF_SEED_LAST` (1..40), handicapped seeds 201..210, the heaviest states of each by the fuzz growth measures, one run-start game and one Duos game. The decks come from the live shipped pools (`spec_for_seed` in `crates/tools/src/golden.rs` deals from the shipped sets, via the fuzz deck streams), so any card addition re-deals the whole corpus. The file says so itself: between two corpora the 1v1 medians moved by up to 1.8x and the Duos ones by up to 5.6x, runner CPUs added another 1.3x, each time budget is 5x the largest of twelve medians, and a budget crossed by a card change that made the corpus heavier is measured again the same way (`perf.rs`, the budget comment). That re-measurement is pure upkeep, and the 5x headroom that absorbs corpus churn also dulls the budgets against real slowdowns. `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` already pins the corpus shape (hotseat states, 2 wide boards, at least one plain, handicapped, run-start and co-op game), so a pinned corpus has a test waiting for it. The repo already knows how to pin deals: `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/` keeps each kept failure's decks and start inputs literally, with a `retired` marker when a patch removes an id.

## Proposal

Check in the corpus inputs (seed, decks, handicaps, deck marks) for the plain range, the handicap range, the run-start game and the Duos game under `crates/tools/perf-corpus/`, one JSON file per game plus a README describing the record shape and the retirement rule copied from the fuzz corpus. `perf.rs` replays those inputs instead of dealing from the live pools; the heaviest-state selection then runs over the replayed games, so it stays deterministic too. Re-measure the medians once after pinning and keep the existing constants unless the pinned corpus moves them. Nothing about the budgets' meaning changes, and engine changes still move the timings (only the deals stop moving).

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` (corpus construction; `crates/tools/README.md` perf row, enforced by `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`)
- new `crates/tools/perf-corpus/` records and README (modelled on `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/README.md`)
- `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` (extend the corpus-shape assertions to the pinned files)
- No SPEC section: the budgets are CLAUDE.md rule 9 constants (`*_BUDGET_*` in `perf.rs`) measured under #3429.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Adding a card to the catalog (e.g. forcing an extra id into the fuzz pool) leaves every pinned corpus file byte-identical and `perf --smoke --json` reports the same corpus games.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf` passes, including a new assertion that each corpus game replays from its pinned file with no refused action.
- [ ] A corpus file holding a removed card id fails the lint with a message naming the `retired` marker to add, mirroring the fuzz corpus.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

## Size and risks

Medium: about a hundred lines plus the corpus files. Risk is staleness if cards are removed (handled by the copied retirement rule) and the one-time re-measurement after pinning, which this issue's own acceptance run performs.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45664526610)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`cargo jackioh perf` replays a checked-in set of pinned games from `crates/tools/perf-corpus/` instead of dealing decks from the live pools. That means adding a card never re-deals the corpus. The pinned games are the ones `perf` plays today: golden seeds 1..40 and 201..210, the run-start game and the Duos co-op game, one JSON file each, plus a README modelled on `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/README.md`. The heaviest-state selection runs over the replayed games, so it stays deterministic.

A record naming a removed card id fails the lint with a message that names the `retired` marker to add. The report lists the replayed games. `perf --pin` is the only code that reads the live pools. It writes a record only for a game with no live record and never rewrites a file.

Budget constants and their meaning do not change.

## Files to touch

| Path | | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` | change | Header and budget-comment prose, new constants, `PerfKind`, `PerfRecord`, `read_corpus`, `lint_record`, `deal`, `pin`, `streams`, `run_start_inputs`. The `play_*` functions take a record, `corpus()` reads the directory, the report gains `games`/`retired`, and there are new unit tests. |
| `crates/tools/perf-corpus/*.json` | new | 52 files written by `perf --pin`, never by hand. |
| `crates/tools/perf-corpus/README.md` | new | Record shape, adding, retiring, running, scope. |
| `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` | change | The smoke test asserts the report's games equal the files on disk. |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | change | The `perf` row (usage spans and corpus description) and one command line in the examples block. |

Do not touch:
- `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `crates/ai`, `crates/run`, `crates/shared`, `apps/`
- `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` or `golden.rs`. A temporary edit to `fuzz.rs` in step 12 is reverted.
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`
- any `*_BUDGET_*` value

No spec section or ruling governs this. It is CLAUDE.md rule 9 (named constants, so `PERF_RUN_START_SEED`/`PERF_COOP_SEED`) and rule 4 (the tools crate may read the disk). There is no patch fragment, because the catalog does not change.

## Steps

0. **Baseline, before any edit.** Run `cargo run -q -p jackioh-tools -- perf --smoke --json > /tmp/perf-before.json` (debug build, the profile `cargo test` uses).

1. **`perf.rs` prose and constants.**
   - Rewrite the module doc's corpus paragraph (lines 1–18): the games are replayed from `perf-corpus/` records (#4924), and only the engine moves the timings.
   - Add after `PERF_HEAVIEST_PER_MEASURE`: `pub const PERF_RUN_START_SEED: u32 = 0;` and `pub const PERF_COOP_SEED: u32 = 1;`, each with a doc line. Reword the `PERF_SEED_*` and `PERF_HANDICAP_SEED_*` docs to "the golden seeds `perf --pin` deals".
   - In the budget comment (lines 74–84), replace "a card change deals the corpus's games again, and between those two corpora …" with a note that those were the two corpora main dealt then, and that since #4924 the corpus is pinned. Drop "or by a card change that made the corpus heavier". Change no number.

2. **Imports.** Add `std::fs`, `std::path::Path` and `anyhow::Context`. Change `serde::Serialize` to `serde::{Deserialize, Serialize}`. Add `jackioh_cards::{CATALOG, shipped_versions}` next to `register_all`, plus `DuosDecks` and `Handicap` to the `jackioh_engine` list.

3. **`Args` and `run`.**
   - Add `#[arg(long, conflicts_with_all = ["smoke", "json"])] pub pin: bool` with the doc "Write a record for each pinned game that has none".
   - In `run`, right after `register_all()`:
     ```rust
     if args.pin {
         let written = pin(Path::new(PERF_CORPUS_DIR))?;
         for name in &written { println!("pinned {name}"); }
         println!("perf --pin: {} record(s) written", written.len());
         return Ok(());
     }
     ```

4. **Record types**, in a new `// The pinned corpus` section before `// The corpus`.
   - `pub const PERF_CORPUS_DIR: &str = concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/perf-corpus");`
   - `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)] #[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")] enum PerfKind { Plain, Handicapped, RunStart, Coop }`. The declaration order is the sort order. `fn as_str(self) -> &'static str` returns `"plain"`, `"handicapped"`, `"run-start"` and `"coop"`.
   - `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", deny_unknown_fields)] struct PerfRecord` with these fields:
     - `kind: PerfKind`
     - `seed: u32`
     - `catalog_version: String`
     - `decks: Option<(Vec<String>, Vec<String>)>`
     - `duos_decks: Option<DuosDecks>`
     - `handicaps: Option<PerPlayerOpt<Handicap>>`
     - `deck_marks: Option<PerPlayerOpt<Vec<DeckMark>>>`
     - `retired: Option<String>`
   - Each `Option` carries `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`.
   - `fn streams(handicapped: bool, seed: u32) -> (String, String, String)` returns the game seed, the policy stream and the order stream under the names `golden::spec_for_seed` gives them:
     - plain: `jackioh-fuzz-{seed}`, `jackioh-fuzz-policy-{seed}`, `jackioh-fuzz-policy-order-{seed}`
     - handicapped: `jackioh-fuzz-handicap-{seed}`, `jackioh-fuzz-handicap-policy-{seed}`, `jackioh-fuzz-handicap-policy-order-{seed}`

5. **`read_corpus` and `lint_record`.** Copy the shape of `fuzz.rs::read_corpus` (lines 3877–3905).
   - `fn read_corpus(dir: &Path) -> Result<(Vec<(String, PerfRecord)>, Vec<String>)>` reads every `.json` file, parses it as a `PerfRecord`, and prefixes each problem with the file name. A parse failure becomes `"{name}: not a perf record: {error}"`.
   - After reading, sort the records by `(kind, seed, catalog_version)`, not by file name. Otherwise `plain-10` sorts before `plain-2` and `corpus()`'s "longest game, lower seed on a tie" rule breaks.
   - Add this check across records: two live (non-retired) records with the same `(kind, seed)` give `"{name}: a second live {kind} record for seed {seed}: retire one"`.
   - `fn lint_record(record: &PerfRecord) -> Vec<String>` checks:
     - `catalogVersion` is in `shipped_versions()`. Otherwise: `catalogVersion "{v}" is no version in crates/cards/patches/patches.json`.
     - A field table `[("decks", present, kind != Coop), ("duosDecks", present, kind == Coop), ("handicaps", present, Handicapped|RunStart), ("deckMarks", present, RunStart)]`. A required field that is absent gives `"{kind} requires {name}"`. A present field that is not required gives `"{kind} cannot set {name}"`.
     - `retired` of `Some` with a blank string gives `retired is empty: say which ids left the catalog and in which patch`.
     - `retired` of `None`: every deck id (both 1v1 decks, or all four of `duosDecks`) must satisfy `CATALOG.contains_key(id)`. Otherwise: `"\"{id}\" names no catalog card: mark the record retired (add \"retired\": \"<which ids, which patch>\"), never edit its decks"`.
   - Engine setup rules (deck sizes, handicaps, marks) are not re-linted; `begin_game` already refuses a bad setup.

6. **`deal` and `pin`.** These are the only code that reads the live pools.
   - `fn run_start_inputs() -> ((Vec<String>, Vec<String>), PerPlayerOpt<Handicap>, PerPlayerOpt<Vec<DeckMark>>)` holds lines 471–486 of today's `play_run_start` verbatim.
   - `fn deal(kind: PerfKind, seed: u32, version: &str) -> Result<PerfRecord>`:
     - Plain/Handicapped: `let spec = spec_for_seed(seed)?;` then `decks: Some(spec.decks)` and `handicaps: spec.handicaps`.
     - RunStart: `run_start_inputs()`.
     - Coop: `duos_decks: Some(duos_decks_for_seed_from(seed, &SHIPPED_FUZZ_POOL))`.
   - `fn pin(dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>>`:
     - `fs::create_dir_all(dir)`.
     - `version` is `shipped_versions().last()`; error if it is empty.
     - `read_corpus(dir)?`; if there are problems, `bail!` listing them (the person adds the retired marker first).
     - The wanted games are `(Plain, k)` for `PERF_SEED_FIRST..=PERF_SEED_LAST`, `(Handicapped, k)` for `PERF_HANDICAP_SEED_FIRST..=PERF_HANDICAP_SEED_LAST`, `(RunStart, PERF_RUN_START_SEED)` and `(Coop, PERF_COOP_SEED)`.
     - Skip a game that has a live record. Otherwise `deal` it and write `serde_json::to_string_pretty(&record)? + "\n"` to `{kind}-{seed}-{version}.json`.
     - If that name exists, try `{kind}-{seed}-{version}-2.json`, then `-3`, and so on. A retired record is never overwritten.
     - Return the written names.

7. **`play_*` take a record.**
   - `play_seed(record: &PerfRecord)`:
     - Replace `spec_for_seed(k)?` with `let (game, policy_stream, order_stream) = streams(record.kind == PerfKind::Handicapped, record.seed);` and `let decks = record.decks.clone().ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("perf-corpus: a {} record has no decks", record.kind.as_str()))?;`.
     - Use `game`, `decks`, `record.handicaps.clone()`, `policy_stream` and `order_stream` where `spec.seed`, `spec.decks`, `spec.handicaps`, `spec.policy` and `spec.order` were.
     - Set `seed: record.seed` in `Played`.
     - Keep `create_game`, the `perf-{n}` nonces and the loop unchanged.
   - `play_run_start(record)`: take decks, handicaps and marks from the record with the same `ok_or_else`. Keep `create_recorded_game`, the literal stream names and the `perf-run-start-{n}` nonces. Set `seed: record.seed`.
   - `play_coop_game(record)`: `seed: format!("perf-duos-{}", record.seed)`, `decks: record.duos_decks.clone().ok_or_else(…)?`. Use `record.seed` where the `seed` argument was.

8. **`corpus()` and the report.**
   - `Corpus` gains `games: Vec<String>`, `retired: Vec<String>` and `seeds: [u32; 2]`.
   - `corpus()` calls `read_corpus(Path::new(PERF_CORPUS_DIR))?` and bails on problems with `"perf-corpus: {n} problem(s):\n{lines}"`. It splits the live records by kind.
   - Plain and Handicapped need at least one live record. Otherwise bail with "perf-corpus has no live {kind} game: `cargo jackioh perf --pin` deals a replacement for each retired one".
   - RunStart and Coop need exactly one, else bail naming the count.
   - Play the plain and handicapped games with `par_iter().map(|r| play_seed(r)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()`.
   - The run-start and co-op games, `take_heaviest*`, `longest` and the fold fields stay as they are.
   - `games` and `retired` are the file names of live and of retired records. `seeds` is the first and last live plain seed.
   - `CorpusCounts` gains `games: Vec<String>` and `retired: Vec<String>` (serialised as `games` and `retired`) and takes `seeds` from the corpus. In `measure()` fill them in from `corpus`.
   - In `perf_table`'s first line, insert `pinned: {} games, {} retired; ` before `forecast:`, using `corpus.games.len()` and `corpus.retired.len()`.

9. **Generate.** Run `cargo run -q -p jackioh-tools -- perf --pin`. `ls crates/tools/perf-corpus/*.json | wc -l` must print 52. Run it again: it must print `0 record(s) written`.

10. **`perf-corpus/README.md`**, modelled on the fuzz one:
    - A field table for the record.
    - Names: `<kind>-<seed>-<catalogVersion>.json`.
    - "Adding a record": `perf --pin`.
    - "Retiring": when a patch removes or renames an id, add `"retired": "<which ids, which patch>"`, never edit the decks, never delete the file, then run `perf --pin` for the replacement.
    - "Running it": `cargo jackioh perf --smoke --json` and `cargo test -p jackioh-tools perf`.
    - "Scope": the deals are pinned, not the logs. A card that draws from an in-game pool (Discover and similar) can still play differently after a pool grows, which is an engine change that moves the timings.

11. **`crates/tools/README.md`.**
    - The `perf` row's first cell becomes `` `perf [--smoke] [--json]`, `perf --pin` `` (`acceptance.rs::table_drift` needs a span naming `--pin`).
    - Describe the corpus as "the pinned games of `perf-corpus/` … each replayed from its record, never dealt from the live pools; `--pin` writes a record for each game the constants name that has none".
    - Add `cargo jackioh perf --pin   # a record for each pinned perf game that lacks one (perf-corpus/)` under the `fuzz --regress` example.

12. **Prove criterion 1 by hand, and revert.**
    - Temporarily set `POOL_EXCLUSIONS` in `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` (line 548) to `&[PoolExclusion { id: "core-001", why: "probe" }]`. This re-deals every unpinned deal.
    - Run `perf --smoke --json > /tmp/perf-after-pool.json`.
    - Restore `fuzz.rs` with Edit; `git diff --stat crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` must be empty.
    - Run `perf --smoke --json > /tmp/perf-after.json`.
    - `jq -S '{corpus: (.corpus|del(.games,.retired)), fold, duosFold}'` on `perf-before.json`, `perf-after.json` and `perf-after-pool.json` must give three identical outputs. The first equality shows the pinned corpus is today's corpus; the second shows a pool change leaves it alone.
    - `git status --porcelain crates/tools/perf-corpus` must show only the new files, none modified.

## Tests

`perf.rs`, `mod tests` (add `use jackioh_cards::shipped_versions;` if missing; temp dirs are `std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("jackioh-perf-<name>-{}", std::process::id()))`, removed at the end):

- `every_dealt_record_round_trips_and_lints_clean`: `deal` for `(Plain,1)`, `(Handicapped,201)`, `(RunStart,0)` and `(Coop,1)` at `shipped_versions().last()`. Each survives `to_string_pretty` then `from_str` unchanged, and `lint_record` returns `[]`.
- `streams_name_the_golden_traces_streams`: for k in 1, 40, 201 and 210, `streams(k >= 201, k)` equals `(spec.seed, spec.policy, spec.order)` of `spec_for_seed(k)`. This proves the pinned games keep today's streams.
- `a_record_naming_a_removed_id_is_told_to_add_the_retired_marker` (criterion 3): write a plain record whose deck holds `"core-gone"` to a temp dir and run `read_corpus`. The problem starts with the file name and contains `"core-gone"`, `retired` and `never edit its decks`. Set `retired: Some("core-gone left the catalog in v0.6.14b".into())` and the lint is clean. Set `Some("  ")` and it contains `retired is empty`.
- `a_record_holds_only_its_kinds_fields`: a plain record with `handicaps` gives `plain cannot set handicaps`. A run-start record without `deckMarks` gives `run-start requires deckMarks`. A coop record with `decks` gives `coop cannot set decks`. A bad `catalogVersion` is named.
- `pin_writes_each_missing_game_once_and_never_rewrites`: `pin` into an empty temp dir writes `(LAST-FIRST+1)+(HLAST-HFIRST+1)+2` files. `read_corpus` has no problems and its first 40 records are Plain with seeds 1..=40 in order. A second `pin` writes 0. Read one record, set `retired`, rewrite it, and run `pin` again: it writes exactly 1 file with the same kind and seed, live and under a different name, and the retired file's bytes are unchanged.
- `the_checked_in_corpus_lints_clean`: `read_corpus(PERF_CORPUS_DIR)` returns no problems and holds at least one live record of each kind.
- Update `the_table_has_a_line_per_measure_under_its_header` for the new `CorpusCounts` fields (`games: vec!["plain-1-v0.6.14b.json".into()]`, `retired: Vec::new()`) and assert `lines[0].contains("pinned: 1 games, 0 retired")`.

`crates/tools/tests/perf.rs`, in `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once` (criterion 2). Read `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/perf-corpus")`, parse each `.json`, and split file names into live and retired by the `retired` key.
- Assert `corpus.games` and `corpus.retired`, each sorted, equal those sets. The exit-0 and `failures == []` asserts already there are the "no refused action" proof, because a refused or divergent action makes `perf` bail.
- Assert at least one live name starts with each of `plain-`, `handicapped-`, `run-start-` and `coop-`.
- Assert `corpus.seeds` equals the min and max `seed` of the live plain files.

Commands:
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools perf`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance`

## Done when

- [ ] `crates/tools/perf-corpus/` holds 52 records plus the README, written only by `perf --pin`.
- [ ] `perf --smoke --json` replays them. The step-12 jq comparison shows a pool change and the pin leave the corpus, fold and Duos fold blocks identical to the baseline.
- [ ] A removed id fails the lint naming the `retired` marker (unit test).
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools` passes, including `--test perf` and `--test acceptance`.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- [ ] `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes, then `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `cargo jackioh patches check` and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass.
- [ ] `fuzz.rs` shows no diff, no `*_BUDGET_*` value changed, and no new `#[allow]` or `#[ignore]`.

## Risks

- **Determinism.** Rayon's indexed `collect` keeps order, and the records are sorted by `(kind, seed, version)`, so ties keep the lower seed. The streams and nonces are copied exactly; the step-0 and step-12 diffs catch any drift.
- **Pinned deals, not logs.** A card that draws from an in-game random pool can still change a replayed game when a pool grows. The README says so; engine changes should move the timings. Pinning the logs would instead turn every rules change into a re-record.
- **Budgets.** The pinned corpus is main's current one, and the budgets carry 5x headroom over the 98bb1823 corpus. Do not edit constants; the bot runner is not GitHub's. A local `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf perf_holds_every_budget -- --ignored` run may be reported, but a slow runner is not a reason to change a budget.
- **CI.** `scripts/ci-scope.sh` has no skip line for `perf-corpus/`, so a PR touching it also runs e2e smoke. That is only extra minutes and is left alone.
- **README contract.** `acceptance.rs::table_drift` fails unless `--pin` appears in a usage span of the `perf` row.
- **Panics.** Use `ok_or_else` and `?`, not `unwrap`. The lint already guarantees the fields exist.

## Open questions

- The one-time re-measurement of the medians on GitHub's runners (twelve runs per profile, per the budget comment) needs a person, or a look at the first daily `perf_holds_every_budget` after merge. It does not block this change, since the budgets stay as they are.
- The judge's note says a pinned corpus freezes new cards out of measurement. `perf --pin` plus a raised `PERF_SEED_LAST` adds games when someone wants new cards covered. No other decision is needed.
````
